title: Multi-Engine Rate of Climb vs Density Altitude and Weight
conditions: Cowl flaps open, full throttle and max RPM, landing gear retracted, mixture adjusted for smooth operation, optimum airspeed, wing flaps retracted

verification.method: Each curve re-measured at 3 independent pixel-calibrated points (sea level, DA=13900 ft, DA=16600 ft) via column-cluster detection with gridlines masked out. All three points fit a straight line to within ~1% (linear least-squares), then extrapolated to ROC=0 for daAtZero. Cross-checked against a direct left-edge (ROC=0 axis) pixel read, which agreed with the fitted intercept within 0.2-0.4% for all three curves.
verification.changeFromOriginal: seaLevel values were already close (within ~3%). daAtZero (service ceiling) was significantly overestimated in the original digitization, worst for the 2800 lb curve (27000 -> 22025 ft, a 23% error) and the 3200 lb curve (23000 -> 21080 ft, 9% error); the 3600 lb curve was closer (20500 -> 20060 ft, 2%). Likely cause: the original digitization misread which of the 4 curves on this chart (the 4th being the unmodeled '3600 lb, gear extended, flaps 15' configuration) terminated where, in the crowded convergence zone near the top of the chart.
verification.confidence: High for all three curves — 3-point fits were highly linear and self-consistent.
